_comment: Single source of truth for the generated data format, read by src/core/constants.js and scripts/data/*.py. Changing an order here changes the meaning of src/data/items.json: re-run `python scripts/data/regen.py` afterwards. `activities`: the boxes of the "Gear from" filter, in the order the page lists them (by section). An item row's routes (field 8) are bit masks over them: bit i = activities[i], bit len(activities) = the market board (tradeable pieces); a piece shows when every bit of one of its routes is allowed (scripts/data/gear_activities.py). `section` groups the boxes in the menu; `on`: ticked by default; `hint`: what the box covers, shown for the box under the pointer, where {currentTomes} is filled from items.json and {capPatch} from the level cap (7.x at level 100). A slot's `blocks` lists the slot types it leaves empty (code 12: a body piece that also covers the head; 13: legs that also cover the feet; 14: a body piece that also covers the hands, legs and feet; a `twoHanded` weapon blocks the off-hand). BaseParam's share columns follow EquipSlotCategory rows in order and their names are the dataminers' own: code 14 (EquipSlotCategory 16) reads the 16th column, named ChestHeadLegsFeetPercent although the piece leaves the head free (440 fits Herklaedi's stats). Slot `percent` is the share of the ItemLevel budget in thousandths; gen_item_level.py checks it against the `baseParamColumn` of every stat row in BaseParam.csv. `crafterGathererParams`: crafter and gatherer stats (BaseParam row id and name); gen_items.py leaves out any piece that carries one, normal or HQ, and stops if a row id no longer has that name.

itemRow._comment: The fields of an item row in items.json, in order: field i is `fields`[i] (docs/engineering/data-pipeline.md, Row format and order). scripts/data/item_format.py reads and builds rows by these names (row_fields), and ROW in src/core/constants.js names the same positions (data-format.test.js checks). The `rowField` of materia, rarity, gameId, levelScaled, category and the damageDefense entries must be the position of its name here (meldSlots, overmeld, rarity, gameId, scales, category, damagePhys ...); gen_items.py stops otherwise.

materia._comment: Melding. Item rows carry two more fields at `rowFields`: meldSlots, the item's `slotColumn` (guaranteed slots, 0 to `maxSlots`; gen_items.py stops above it), and overmeld, 1 when its `overmeldColumn` is True (overmelding allowed). The materia table in items.json ({values, gate, high}, one entry per grade I to `grades`) comes from the `sheet` rows whose `statColumn` is one of `statKeys` (BaseParam row ids from `stats`) and whose `itemColumn`[0] is non-zero; rows with values but no items are decoys and are skipped. The rows must agree: values from `valueColumn`[0..grades-1], gate = the `gateColumn` (Item.csv) of each grade's materia item, item and value columns past the last grade all 0, gates non-decreasing. high: the grades whose `highColumn` in `gradeSheet` (row = grade - 1) is 0, which must be the grades worth more than each neighbouring grade.

rarity._comment: Item rows carry the item's `itemColumn` (Item.csv: 1 white, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 purple, 7 pink) at `rowField`; gen_items.py stops on a value that is not a whole number. Used by the accuracy check: green crafted healer gear carries its Direct Hit line at a higher share (formulas.js predictRaw).

gameId._comment: Item rows carry the item's game id (Item.csv row `itemColumn`) at `rowField`, so a piece can be matched with other tools and links that name items by id (ffxiv-gearing, xivgear). gen_items.py stops on an id that is not a whole number or appears twice.

levelScaled._comment: Item rows carry 1 at `rowField` when the item's `itemColumn` (Item.csv) is `value`, else 0: gear whose item level and stats follow the wearer's level (the game's description reads "IL and attributes synced to current job level."; level 89 and 99 boost gear, gift earrings and rings). Below the level its item level is for, such a piece is synced to that level's item level whatever its equip level (sync-target.js). gen_items.py stops on a value outside `known`.

category._comment: Item rows carry the piece's gear category (gear_categories.py: Item.SubcategorySort refined by shop data; every code in docs/engineering/subcategory-sort-codes.md) at `rowField`, as an index into `list`. The page shows its label on each piece, so a player can see where it comes from. `list` must hold every category a kept piece can have (gear_categories.CATEGORIES minus LEFT_OUT) exactly once, and nothing else; gen_items.py stops otherwise.

damageDefense._comment: Weapon damage and defense (docs/mechanics/math.md, section 4). Item rows carry each entry's value at `rowField`: the Item.csv `itemColumn`, plus, when the item can be HQ (CanBeHq), its HQ bonus (a BaseParamSpecial pair whose stat is `baseParam`). Zero on pieces without it (weapon damage on armor, defense on weapons and accessories). gen_item_level.py writes, per entry, the `itemLevelColumn` of ItemLevel.csv to IL, the `baseParam` row's MeldParam percents to MP and its slot share per slot code (each slot's `baseParamColumn`) to SHARES, so a synced value is capped like a stat (formulas.js capValue). Not in `stats`: their slot shares differ from the stats' (weapon damage 1000 on weapons only; defense 176/236 on armor, 0 on accessories).

statFactor._comment: Per-item stat factor. Field 9 of an item row is the item's `itemColumn` (Item.csv), an index 0..count-1 into the `baseParamColumn`[0..count-1] columns of BaseParam.csv. Each stat's BaseParam row holds there the percent its full-share slot value is multiplied by on that kind of item (Vitality 90 on Intelligence/Mind gear, every main stat 90 on gear that carries all four). gen_item_level.py writes the table to item-level.json (MP); gen_items.py stops on an index outside it.

jobModifiers._comment: Each job's attribute modifiers, for item-level.json's JOBS (gen_item_level.py): the ClassJob.csv column of each attribute key (stat keys above), in percent. A character's base attribute is floor(the level's main stat base x modifier / 100) plus the clan's bonus (docs/mechanics/math.md, Totals as on the character panel).

food._comment: Meals, for food.json (gen_food.py). A meal is an Item.csv row whose `uiCategoryColumn` is `uiCategory` (Meal); its `actionColumn` names an ItemAction row whose Action is one of `actions` and whose Data[0] is `status` (Well Fed). That row's `foodRowColumn` is the ItemFood row: up to three stats (BaseParam[i], IsRelative[i], ValueHQ[i] percent, MaxHQ[i] cap). Kept: HQ-able meals whose stats are all relative and all in `stats` (raw stat keys from `stats` above), with at least one substat; carried: HQ values of every substat, and of Vitality (`vitality`) apart from them. Medicine (tinctures) uses ItemFood too but another category and action.
